dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. Good afternoon.
Hello. Yes, good afternoon. I am calling about snow plowing. The plow came down my street earlier, but I think it did not finish the job. I would like to ask if it can come back.
Sure, I can take that down. What street are you on?
I am at 81 Rhode Island Avenue. In the Historic Hill area. It is not far from the corner, maybe two houses down.
Eighty-one Rhode Island Avenue. Okay. And what's going on there, exactly? Is the street not cleared at all, or is it partly done?

It is partly done. The plow went through one time, I think in the morning. It pushed the snow to the side, so now there is a hard bank at the edge of the road. And, um, it is across the bottom of the sidewalk ramp and in front of the next house.
Okay, so a bank of snow pushed up along the curb, blocking the end of the walkway.

Yes, exactly. My neighbor is the one I am worried about. She is elderly, she lives alone in the house next to mine. She cannot get out right now. She does not have a way to climb over this snow, and her steps lead right to that spot. She needs a path, at least a narrow one, so she can get to the street if someone has to come for her.
Understood. Is she okay otherwise? Does she need any kind of help right now, like an emergency?

No, no emergency. She is fine. She has food and she is warm. I checked this morning. It is only the path. I shoveled her steps and her walkway, but the bank at the street is too heavy and too high for me to move today. It is packed, you know, from the plow.
Yeah, that stuff is like concrete when it's been pushed. Alright, so what you're asking is for a plow to come back down that stretch and open it up.
Yes. Come back, and if the driver can clear the bottom of the ramp, even a little, that would help. I do not know if that is possible. I am only asking.

I'll put it in as a request for a return pass, and I'll note the neighbor on the ticket so the crew knows there's someone who can't get out. I can't tell you exactly when they'll get there. They're working through the whole city on a rotation.
That is fine. I understand. It is a normal winter day, I know there are many streets. I just want it on the list.

It'll be on the list. Let me read back what I have. Eighty-one Rhode Island Avenue, Historic Hill, plow came through but left a packed bank at the curb blocking the end of the walkway, and the elderly neighbor next door can't get out. Did I get that right?

Yes, that is right. Except one detail. Her house is the one on the left side, if you are facing from the street. Number seventy-nine, I believe. But I am not fully sure of the number, so please say next door to eighty-one.
Okay, next door to eighty-one, left side as you face the house. I'll put it that way so there's no mix-up.
Good. Thank you.
Do you want a call back if there's an update? I'd have your number, but let me make sure I have it right.
Yes. It is four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-nine-six. It is my cell phone, so it should reach me.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-nine-six. And your name?
Luz Valdez. L-U-Z, and then Valdez, V-A-L-D-E-Z.

Got it, Luz Valdez. Now, in the meantime, if you can, leave the part you shoveled as clear as you can and, if you have any room, keep a spot cleared by the curb so the driver can see where the opening is.
I can do that. I will make a small marker. Honestly, I am staying here this year anyway. We decided to skip our vacation to build up some savings, so I have time. I can keep watching the street.
Well, that works out for your neighbor, at least. Alright, Luz, the request is in. If the crew has questions they may call you.
That is fine. I will answer. Thank you for your help, Lorraine.
You're welcome. Take care, and happy holidays.
Thank you. You too. Goodbye.
